The overall objective of the programme is to enhance the protection of so-called “People on the Move”—individuals forced to flee due to conflict, violence, or humanitarian crises. Through an integrated approach, the programme aims not only to provide immediate protection but also to contribute to structural solutions that strengthen the resilience of individuals and communities. Result 1 – Direct Protection: Providing immediate assistance to victims of violence, with particular attention to gender-based violence (GBV) and child protection. This includes medical, psychosocial, and legal support, as well as the distribution of dignity kits and school materials. Result 2 – Reduction of Vulnerabilities: Addressing the root causes of protection gaps through awareness-raising, capacity building, food security, and improved access to shelter and basic services. Strengthening social cohesion and promoting peaceful coexistence enhances community resilience. Result 3 – Crisis Response: Delivering rapid and coordinated emergency assistance in response to sudden disasters or escalations of violence, with a response time of 72 hours (48 hours in the DRC) and implementation within 30 days. Result 4 – Local Capacity Strengthening: Strengthening the technical, organizational, and humanitarian capacities of local Caritas partners and other actors, in line with localization principles and sustainable humanitarian action.
